0.long_answer: The defect is agenesis of the corpus callosum. In individuals with Infantile Spasms-Broad Thumbs Syndrome, this rare congenital malformation is characterized by the incomplete or absent formation of the corpus callosum, the major bundle of nerve fibers that connects the two cerebral hemispheres. The Probst bundles, which are aberrant bundles of white matter, form as a result of misdirected axonal growth because the usual target, the corpus callosum, is missing. This distinctive imaging finding helps to identify the underlying developmental anomaly in affected individuals.
